glossary.definition: Machine learning is the broader field of teaching computers to spot patterns in data and get better at a task through experience, instead of a programmer writing out every rule by hand. It's the difference between hard-coding "if the email contains the word 'lottery,' mark it spam" versus showing the computer thousands of real spam and non-spam emails and letting it work out the patterns itself. Modern AI, including every LLM, is a product built on machine learning techniques.

items.title: VCs bet $30M on Larridin’s ability to help enterprises demonstrate AI’s value for money
items.summary: As enterprises ramp up their spending on artificial intelligence tools, it’s only right for senior executives to want to know exactly what they’re getting in return for their costly investments. Larridin Inc. , a startup focused on AI adoption measurement, has just raised $30 million in Series A funding to try and provide them with the answers. Today’s round was led by Pelion Ventures and saw participation from existing backers Andreessen Horowitz and Gradient Ventures, as well as new investors like GFT, W23, Thayer, DG Daiwa Ventures, Cougar Capital and Alumni Ventures.

items.title: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps
items.summary: Apple hinted at ways that it could spur revenue through third-party "opportunities" during its Monday night earnings call. Apple’s services business remains at record levels, but it’s facing growing pressure . The central part of that business, Apple’s App Store, has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming, which have hurt services growth . However, on Monday’s earnings call, Apple signaled that it may look to boost services revenue through third-party apps.

items.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens
items.summary: Y Combinator Garry Tan has jokingly admitted that he's suffered from "cyber psychosis” and barely sleeps sometimes because he’s so excited to be working with his AI agents. On a new episode of Walter Isaacson’s podcast, The Builders, Tan put a price tag on his passion. Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan has, in the past, jokingly admitted that he’s suffered from “cyber psychosis” and sometimes barely sleeps because he’s so excited to be working with his AI agents. “I spend about maybe $100[,000] to $200,000 a year on tokens,” he told Isaacson.

items.title: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
items.summary: Goldman Sachs is pulling AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot from traders and bankers, limiting access to engineers only. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti publicly praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Now the bank cites "productivity and risk management" as the reason for the reversal. Goldman Sachs has cut off most of its employees from advanced AI coding tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub.

items.title: Anthropic clamps down on Claude’s AI video game clones
items.summary: Anthropic has updated Claude Code's system prompt to prevent the AI tool from being used to re-create existing video games, as reported by Tom's Hardware . Retro gaming is currently being overrun with AI-made decompilations, recompilations, and ports , but while Anthropic will still let people use Claude Code to make games, it doesn't want people to use it for direct clones. Last week, a user on X posted a screenshot allegedly showing two new sentences added to Claude Code's system prompt: "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Anthropic is steering Claude away from re-creating specific titles, but users can still use it to make their own games.

items.title: Google Genie 4 brings world models closer to robot and AI testing
items.summary: The updated version points to new uses for world models in robotics and AI testing, but enterprises must weigh their potential against accuracy gaps.

items.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
items.summary: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement.

items.title: Anthropic Posts $17 Bn in Q3 Revenue, Swings to Operating Loss
items.summary: Anthropic generated $17 billion in revenue in Q3 2026, up from $11.6 billion in the previous quarter. But it recorded an operating loss of $567 million. The company shared its July to September financials in updated filings ahead of its planned IPO. Revenue increased more than 12 times from approximately $1.4 billion year-on-year, but performance reversed from a $974 million profit in Q2 to a loss in Q3 Anthropic attributed the latest quarter’s operating loss partly to its reliance on short-term computing capacity.

items.title: Windows 11 upgrades stall amid ‘chipflation’ and ‘RAMageddon’
items.summary: Microsoft ended mainstream Windows 10 support a year ago, but PC upgrades to Windows 11 have ground to a halt, analysts said. Relief may not come until 2028 or even 2029, as high CPU prices, which analysts call “chipflation,” and high memory prices, widely known as the “RAMpocalypse” or “RAMageddon,” keep PC prices up. PC prices were already high, and recent steps like Intel raising CPU prices are increasing the base cost of PCs, said Dean McCarron, principal analyst at Mercury Research. “When prices are higher, demand goes down.

items.title: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
items.summary: Chatbots are often quite good at retrieving the information you want from the web. But sometimes you’ll get better results by typing your query into a good old search engine. If you've interacted with the likes of Claude , ChatGPT , and Gemini , you've noticed that in addition to everything else they do, these AI chatbots can search the web for you. Depending on what you’re looking for, it can be easier to find more relevant results through a chatbot, which may explain why Google is so keen to push AI Mode for its own search engine.

items.title: Cursor removes malicious Claude Code extension after SSH backdoor attempt
items.summary: A malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension distributed through the Cursor marketplace attempted to install a persistent Secure Shell (SSH) backdoor on developers’ machines, potentially giving attackers remote access to systems holding source code, credentials and other sensitive information. “Between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace,” Cursor said in a security notice . 313, after discovering they had been available in its VS Code extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29. The company said the malicious code attempted to add an attacker-controlled SSH key, enable local SSH access, and establish a reverse tunnel to an attacker-controlled server.

items.title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
items.summary: As debate and legal argument continue over the extent to which developers of large language models are entitled to feed the world’s data into their systems without paying for it, India’s government has come up with an idea to regulate and secure the flow of information. India’s motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because it thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure owners of data stay in control. ” The scheme envisions “Training Data Providers” (TDPs) – examples of which include hospitals, banks, and government agencies – sharing anonymized and encrypted data with a “Data Exchange Platform” (DEP). Entities called “Training Data Consumers” (TDCs) access the data stored at the DEPs to train their models.
